title: Live bootleg recordings keep the band alive
summary: He agrees recordings made at La Conga and elsewhere educate the public, like showing a diamond rather than keeping it in a vault.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: I see. Okay, a lot of band leaders do not like people to record them live because they fear that a bootleg record is going to come out years later. Yet you have been one of the few, along with Jose Curbelo and Noro Morales, who were recorded live years ago at La Conga club, the China Doll and other places like that. The Band Box, La Bamba, and you did more live recordings which are now bootleg records and tapes out there. They have helped keep you alive and out there because WBAI and WKCR have played a lot of these things and the young generation has not heard them and they enjoy it with the stories attached to it. Now, because of this happening, don't you believe that you have benefited by this?
Definitely. Listen, whoever record our music

and play it over the radio or even play it in a party, they 're helping us, they're educating the people that are in the party or educating the people that listen to the radio station. Is no such a thing that you could have a diamond in the vault in the bank and the people will know that you have that three-karat diamond or whatever you have. You have to take a chance that somebody take it away from you and show the diamond.
